text: Commit hygiene: always stage, then review 'git diff --cached --name-status' in a separate step, then commit. On 2026-09-26 a previously 'git rm'-staged file (server/ai-proxy.ts) was swept into an unrelated commit (cd7ab30) because staging+stat+commit ran in one command. Candidate deterministic control: a pre-commit hook or ops.mjs commit helper that refuses to commit when staged paths fall outside the declared cluster path set.

scripts/naming/technical-naming-census.mjs isPtProse() requires a raw score >=2 before flagging a comment/test-title as Portuguese prose. This let at least 21 real Portuguese test titles (describe/it in apps/api and apps/web, e.g. "AdminDashboard — falha de query nunca vira KPI zerado fabricado") pass --check as testTitle candidates:0 because they contained only one weak PT_PROSE function word (e.g. only 'nunca') and no PT_TOKENS lexicon noun and no accented character. Found via a manual second-pass broad regex scan during Cluster Zero Z4 closure (mission-a5c14661), not by the tool itself. Recommend: add a PT_STRONG entry for common unmarked verbs already seen in the wild (executa, grava, registra, atualiza, verifica, confirma, concede, popula, produz) and/or lower the prose threshold specifically for describe/it/test string arguments (shorter, higher-precision strings than free-form comments) so a single unambiguous PT verb is sufficient.

completion-gate.mjs / gate-engine.mjs's workspaceFingerprint appears to bind to something that changes on every commit (likely includes HEAD or the ops state.json content itself), so PASS evidence captured and committed together always reads as 'stale or failing' again immediately after that very commit lands (observed mission-a5c14661, Cluster Zero Z1-Z5 closure 2026-09-27: re-verified+committed at HEAD 1fab009, then the ops-state-only commit 7c6b959 that recorded that evidence made the gate report all 5 criteria stale again, even though zero source files changed between the two commits). This creates an unavoidable one-commit lag between 'genuinely fresh evidence' and 'gate agrees it's fresh' for any criterion whose evidence is committed alongside itself. Recommend: exclude .claude/ops/** from the fingerprint's tracked-tree hash (evidence/state bookkeeping isn't product code under test), or fingerprint working-tree content only (not HEAD), so recording evidence doesn't retroactively invalidate itself.

In this environment, a nested 'claude -p --agent <name>' subprocess (used as a workaround for STRICT_MULTI_AGENT dispatch when the orchestrator session has no native Task/agent-launch tool -- see p0-classify-vars.json's dispatch field from an earlier session, and this session's own use of it for security-reviewer/repo-intelligence/git-auditor) gets a MORE restrictive sandbox than the parent session: read/search tools (ls/grep/wc/Read) work, but code-interpreter execution (node -e, python3 -c, and by extension node scripts/naming/technical-naming-census.mjs --report) was rejected at the tool-permission layer with no interactive user available to approve it, even though the identical command worked fine when run directly by the top-level orchestrator in the same workspace. This silently degrades a dispatched agent from 'can independently verify' to 'can only grep/read', which the agent itself has to notice and flag (as repo-intelligence did here) rather than something the runtime enforces or warns about up front. Recommend: either make nested claude -p sessions inherit the parent's already-granted permission/trust state for this workspace (it currently prints 'Ignoring 5 permissions.allow entries ... workspace has not been trusted' even though the parent session is clearly already trusted and operating in it), or have ops.mjs/completion-gate detect and reject review evidence produced by a permission-degraded nested session.

Explicit owner correction (2026-09-27): Git governance is dev-only. The single authorized branch is dev and the single push target is origin/dev; creating any branch (claude/*, feature, fix, backup, agent or worktree branches) is forbidden, and a runtime-assigned 'designated branch' never overrides owner policy. This session worked and pushed on the runtime branch claude/exciting-wozniak-be642d; its 9 commits were fast-forwarded into dev (ancestry proven after un-shallowing the clone), validated (naming/schema census, typecheck, lint, api 328/2828, web 134/964) and pushed to origin/dev; the local branch was deleted, the remote ref deletion is blocked by the session git gateway (send-pack disconnect on ref delete; no connector delete-ref tool). Enforcement candidate: a deterministic pre-push/pre-commit hook in .claude/settings (hooks) that refuses any git commit/push/branch/switch -c/worktree add when the current branch is not dev or the push destination is not origin/dev, instead of prose only; and the orchestration rules should forbid worktree-isolated agents in this repository (serial execution on dev).

Blind-rename incident (CZ-038): a line-anchored sed ('| "outro";' -> '| "other";') on a shared multi-enum file changed 8 unrelated union types; and a word-boundary regex rename of a column name (pagador) changed PT-BR label text ('Responsável pagador'). Rule candidate: renames in shared files must be scoped to the exact declaration block/AST node, and JSX text/labels must be excluded from identifier regex renames; verify with git diff -U0 on shared files before commit.
